header: The sums behind the converter card, which is laid out like Google's: a kind (Power), a value and unit on the left, the result and unit on the right, and a formula line under them. I keep it pure: it picks units from the tables of units.ts and currency.ts and does the arithmetic. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere.

symbols.name: KIND_NAMES
symbols.sig: const KIND_NAMES: Record<ConvKind, string> = { length: "Length", area: "Area", volume: "Volume", mass: "Mass", temperature: "Temperature", angle: "Angle", energy: …

symbols.name: optionsFor
doc: Returns the units of a kind, as the two dropdowns list them ("Mechanical horsepower", "Metric horsepower (PS)", "US dollar (USD)").

symbols.name: DEFAULT_PAIRS
symbols.sig: const DEFAULT_PAIRS: Partial<Record<ConvKind, [string, string]>> = { currency: ["USD", "INR"], colour: ["rgb", "hex"], power: ["hp", "kW"], engine: ["hp", "ps"], temperature: ["C", "F"] }
doc: The pair a kind opens with: Google's is metre to foot, mine is the most useful for the plant.

symbols.name: plainNumber
symbols.sig: export function plainNumber(x: number, sig = 8): string
doc: I write a number for an input box with up to `sig` significant digits (Google shows six), no grouping and no trailing zeros ("1.01387", "0.621371").

symbols.name: boxNumber
symbols.sig: export function boxNumber(kind: ConvKind, x: number): string
doc: The result box shows six significant digits like Google; I show money to the paisa (or four digits when below one).

members.name: formula
doc: I put this line under the boxes: "For an approximate result, multiply the power value by 1.0139"

members.name: notes
doc: Notes I add when a unit word has more than one meaning, or to give the rates' date

symbols.name: compute
symbols.sig: export function compute(kind: ConvKind, value: number, fromId: string, toId: string, rates: Rates | null): Computed | null
doc: Returns `value` of `fromId` expressed in `toId`; I return null when a unit is unknown or, for currency, the rate is missing.

members.name: meaning
doc: Here I say what the letters stand for, and what the unit is

symbols.name: ENGINE_UNITS
symbols.sig: const ENGINE_UNITS: EngineUnit[] = [ { id: "ps", short: "PS", name: "Pferdestärke (metric horsepower)", meaning: "PS is short for the German word Pferdes …
doc: The three ways a vehicle's engine power is quoted today; I list them in the order they read from the largest number to the smallest for the same power.

symbols.name: engineRows
symbols.sig: export function engineRows(value: number, atId: string): Array<{ id: string; short: string; value: number }> | null
symbols.returns: Array<{ id: string; short: string; value: number }> | null
doc: Gives the value in each of the three units, from a value typed in one of them; I list PS first, then bhp, then kW.

symbols.name: ENGINE_WORD
symbols.sig: const ENGINE_WORD: Record<string, string> = { ps: "ps", cv: "ps", bhp: "hp", hp: "hp", kw: "kW" }

symbols.name: parseEngine
symbols.sig: export function parseEngine(raw: string): { value: number; id: string } | null
doc: "engine power", "100 bhp", "ps bhp kw", "bhp vs ps vs kw": I treat these as a question about engine power that is not a plain two-unit conversion.

behaviours: the Google example: 1 bhp is 1.01387 PS and the formula says multiply by 1.0139
a temperature has a formula of its own
a temperature is converted both ways
currency needs the rates and says the rate and the date
money is shown to the paisa, other results to six digits
typing a result back gives the first value (both boxes are editable)
every kind has at least two units and a default pair that exists (colour is the one kind that is not a pair of units: it has its own panel, RGB and HEX)
an unknown unit or a bad number gives nothing
numbers for the boxes have no grouping and no trailing zeros
engine power: 1 bhp is 1.01387 PS and 0.7457 kW, listed PS first, then bhp, then kW
engine power: the same power gives the largest number in PS, then bhp, then kW, whichever unit is typed
engine power: 100 kW is 134.1 bhp and 135.96 PS; and PS is explained as the German Pferdestärke
engine power questions: '100 bhp', 'ps bhp kw', 'engine power', 'bhp vs ps vs kw' are read; a lone unit, a repeat or a sentence is not
the engine kind has three options and its default pair
